related_work_framing.close_neighbor: WriteBack-RAG-style amortization writes derived evidence, summaries, or answers back into an external memory/KB so later queries retrieve the augmented corpus.
related_work_framing.current_project_scope: This project distills expensive grounded behavior into model/scaffold training data and preference data while keeping the evaluation evidence pack fixed and citation-auditable.
related_work_framing.exclusion_reason: A mutable write-back memory changes the retrieval corpus and can leak final-window facts unless it is built strictly from prior dated/private snapshots. The current QASPER/arXiv result still has no full write-back baseline; the git-doc snapshot diagnostic is a toy versioned-domain check, not a replacement for the paper-critical Qwen 3B trained-student evaluation.

current_artifacts.role: Distills a combined support policy into SFT/verifier rows. It does not write derived facts back into a retrievable KB.
Exports mini-negative support labels for post-training/verifier training, not a persistent retrieval memory.
Converts prior-window judged support outcomes into labels; downstream use is model training, not KB rewriting.

support_contrast_prep.role: Creates SFT/preference rows from judged support failures; it is a model-training packet rather than a retrievable KB update.

joint_action_gpu_prep.role: Creates SFT/DPO rows for a joint keep/repair/abstain policy; it still trains a student rather than writing an evidence memory.

versioned_writeback_diagnostic.interpretation: Write-back memory is a valid competing amortization family only when records are created from prior snapshots. Train-only memory helps stable facts but cannot replace live retrieval for new updates; eval-written memory leaks future facts and over-answers stale train-snapshot queries.

scoped_exclusion.decision: Keep WriteBack-RAG scoped out as a required QASPER baseline for the current artifact set, while retaining the versioned git-doc diagnostic as evidence about leakage-safe write-back behavior.
why_not_counted_as_implemented_baseline: No artifact creates a persistent derived-memory index that is retrieved at inference time.
Existing exports are answer/verifier/preference labels whose provenance remains in training files, not new KB records.
A write-back memory built from final-window judged outputs would leak evaluation answers into retrieval.
A fair write-back comparison needs trusted dated/private KB snapshots so derived records can be written only from past knowledge states.
future_baseline_requirements: Build write-back records only from train-window teacher traces or judged supported answers, never from validation/final-window judgments.
Store each derived record with source document ids, evidence ids, creation date, source run id, and citation provenance.
Retrieve original KB evidence and write-back records together on validation/final windows, while preventing paper/document overlap leakage.
Require final answers to cite original evidence ids or write-back record ids that themselves cite original evidence.
Judge answer support, abstention support, citation support, and total inference cost against the same final-window protocol.

paper_implication: The paper can discuss WriteBack-RAG as a competing amortization family and include the git-doc diagnostic as a small leakage-safe snapshot check, but current claims should remain scoped to post-training data/scaffold distillation until a full write-back baseline is run on a natural dated/private KB benchmark.

llm_budget.note: This scoping artifact reuses local metadata and makes no API calls or GPU jobs.
